content.text:
Act as the design sub-agent for this task.

Design a practical initial Bend 2 Vulkan wrapper like Rust ash in empty /home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan. User requires Giulio2002/bend-collections src/math/u64.bend U64{lo:U32,hi:U32}. Installed Bend 2.0.37; run bend guide before Bend. Linux Vulkan headers and libvulkan, glslangValidator available. Bend effects: def Entry.load()->IO(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,Entry>): import "./native.c"; import "./native.js". C spliced into compiled program, runtime io_node(e,CID(K),a,b), io_tup, io_done/io_fail, io_cstr and io_eff(CID(Entry.load),fn,0). FFI custom opaque handle types NOT supported (only Base File/Socket etc), so do not invent opaque foreign types. User-defined Type or Data constructor wrapping U64 can cross normal constructor ABI. Need ash Entry/Instance/Device dispatch, explicit Vulkan errors, structs/configs and true 64-bit sizes, real native integration (headless discovery/device/buffer memory roundtrip minimum); scalable generated binding path desirable, honest limited initial scope, avoid toy facade or entire renderer. JS may fail clearly native-only. Need laws in LAWS.bend and PROOF.bend. Native GPU Vulkan work sequential effects; parallelize independent pure work where useful. Read /home/aivv/.agents/skills/architect/references/runner-prompt.md and rationale-template.md; you are one of three already managed design runners, do NOT recurse into architect/arena or spawn agents. Artifact only design.md ~100 lines at /tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-2/design.md. Usage first, type/signature sketch, module layout, explicit ownership/FFI handling (no unsafe pointer forging from constructors), error cleanup and design alternatives. No repo edits.
I’ll read the design-runner guidance and Bend guide, then write the proposal to the requested temporary path without changing the repository.

The design can use ordinary `U64` constructors for handles while C keeps the Vulkan handles and dispatch tables in a validated registry. That avoids trusting caller-supplied integers as pointers. I’m applying the architect runner and technical-writing guidance to keep the proposal focused on discovery, device creation, and an explicit buffer-memory roundtrip.

The proposal now includes explicit Vulkan operations and an optional `Entry.with` helper that cleans up on a returned error. Mapped pointers stay in C; Bend receives a checked mapping token with byte-copy operations. The first milestone will prove a host memory roundtrip on a real Vulkan device, with GPU submission left as a later extension.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-2/design.md
+# Bend Vulkan: checked tokens and explicit dispatch
+
+## Usage (caller's view)
+
+The first release supports Linux Vulkan 1.0 discovery, logical devices, buffers, allocation, binding, and coherent host mapping. It keeps ash's Entry/Instance/Device division. It does not claim rendering or GPU execution support.
+The following are call-site pseudocode. `checked` means matching `Done` or returning `Fail` from the callback. These are not executable Bend examples.
+
+```text
+import ./src/vulkan.bend as Vk
+import ./deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
+# Discovery callback passed to Entry.with; the helper always closes its entry.
+instance = checked(Entry.create_instance(entry, InstanceInfo.default()))
+devices = checked(Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance))
+properties = checked(Instance.physical_device_properties(instance, physical))
+# physical comes from devices; an empty list is a valid discovery result.
+```
+
+```text
+# Allocation callback; queue family and memory types come from physical-device queries.
+device = checked(Instance.create_device(instance, physical, DeviceInfo{family, 1}))
+buffer = checked(Device.create_buffer(device, BufferInfo{W.U64{4096, 0}, transfer_src}))
+requirements = checked(Device.buffer_memory_requirements(device, buffer))
+index = checked(Memory.choose_type(memory_types, requirements.type_bits, host_visible_coherent))
+memory = checked(Device.allocate_memory(device, AllocateInfo{requirements.size, index}))
+checked(Device.bind_buffer_memory(device, buffer, memory, W.zero()))
+mapping = checked(Device.map_memory(device, memory, W.zero(), requirements.size))
+checked(Mapping.write_bytes(mapping, W.zero(), [0, 127, 255]))
+bytes = checked(Mapping.read_bytes(mapping, W.zero(), 3)) # require exactly [0, 127, 255]
+checked(Device.unmap_memory(device, mapping))
+checked(Device.destroy_buffer(device, buffer)); checked(Device.free_memory(device, memory))
+checked(Instance.destroy_device(instance, device)); checked(Entry.destroy_instance(entry, instance))
+```
+
+Each callback returns `IO(VkResult<A>)`. `Entry.with` handles cleanup after either result. Every operation above also works without that helper, with explicit `Entry.close`.
+
+## Problem
+
+Bend 2.0.37 supports custom effects but cannot introduce opaque foreign handle types. Constructors can carry identifiers, but callers can construct identifiers themselves. The C boundary must validate those identifiers before touching driver objects. Affine values can also be dropped, so `Type` alone cannot promise resource destruction.
+Use the required [bend-collections U64](https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend-collections/blob/main/src/math/u64.bend), pinned to commit `bc78c4f4cabb536a2a1dd6e308b6a8f0afafda7c`. Import its `W.U64{lo: U32, hi: U32}` directly. Do not create another integer implementation.
+
+## Shape
+
+The sketch uses `VkResult<A>` as shorthand for `Result<&1, &1, Error, A>` and `Bytes` for `List<&2, U32>`. Each signature names the intended contract, with implementation bodies omitted.
+
+```text
+type Entry is Data: Entry{id: W.U64}
+type Instance is Data: Instance{id: W.U64}
+type PhysicalDevice is Data: PhysicalDevice{id: W.U64}
+type Device is Data: Device{id: W.U64}
+type Buffer is Data: Buffer{id: W.U64}
+type DeviceMemory is Data: DeviceMemory{id: W.U64}
+type Mapping is Data: Mapping{id: W.U64}
+type ErrorKind is Data: Vulkan{} | Loader{} | InvalidHandle{} | InvalidConfig{} | Unsupported{} | Cleanup{}
+type Error is Data: Error{kind: ErrorKind, code: U32, operation: String, detail: String}
+type InstanceInfo is Data: InstanceInfo{application: String, api_version: U32, layers: +List<String>, extensions: +List<String>}
+type DeviceInfo is Data: DeviceInfo{queue_family: U32, queue_count: U32}
+type BufferUsage is Data: BufferUsage{bits: U32}
+type MemoryFlags is Data: MemoryFlags{bits: U32}
+type BufferInfo is Data: BufferInfo{size: W.U64, usage: BufferUsage}
+type AllocateInfo is Data: AllocateInfo{size: W.U64, memory_type_index: U32}
+type MemoryRequirements is Data: MemoryRequirements{size: W.U64, alignment: W.U64, type_bits: U32}
+Entry.load() -> IO(VkResult<Entry>)
+Entry.with(-A: Type, body: Entry -> IO(VkResult<A>)) -> IO(VkResult<A>)
+Entry.create_instance(entry: Entry, info: InstanceInfo) -> IO(VkResult<Instance>)
+Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(instance: Instance) -> IO(VkResult<List<PhysicalDevice>>)
+Instance.physical_device_properties(instance: Instance, physical: PhysicalDevice) -> IO(VkResult<PhysicalDeviceProperties>)
+Instance.queue_family_properties(instance: Instance, physical: PhysicalDevice) -> IO(VkResult<List<QueueFamilyProperties>>)
+Instance.memory_properties(instance: Instance, physical: PhysicalDevice) -> IO(VkResult<MemoryProperties>)
+Instance.create_device(instance: Instance, physical: PhysicalDevice, info: DeviceInfo) -> IO(VkResult<Device>)
+Device.create_buffer(device: Device, info: BufferInfo) -> IO(VkResult<Buffer>)
+Device.buffer_memory_requirements(device: Device, buffer: Buffer) -> IO(VkResult<MemoryRequirements>)
+Memory.choose_type(types: List<MemoryType>, allowed: U32, flags: MemoryFlags) -> VkResult<U32>
+Device.allocate_memory(device: Device, info: AllocateInfo) -> IO(VkResult<DeviceMemory>)
+Device.bind_buffer_memory(device: Device, buffer: Buffer, memory: DeviceMemory, offset: W.U64) -> IO(VkResult<Unit>)
+Device.map_memory(device: Device, memory: DeviceMemory, offset: W.U64, size: W.U64) -> IO(VkResult<Mapping>)
+Mapping.write_bytes(mapping: Mapping, offset: W.U64, bytes: Bytes) -> IO(VkResult<Unit>)
+Mapping.read_bytes(mapping: Mapping, offset: W.U64, count: U32) -> IO(VkResult<Bytes>)
+```
+
+Query records contain named Vulkan fields, including device name/type/API version, queue counts/flags, and memory types/heaps with U64 heap sizes. Include `InstanceInfo.default() -> InstanceInfo`. The cleanup calls shown in usage and `Entry.close(entry)` all return `IO(VkResult<Unit>)`.
+Data wrappers allow normal Bend reuse through `+` bindings without threading an owner through every query. Distinct constructor types catch accidental handle mixing. C enforces liveness, parentage, and state, per boundary-discipline. The interface hides dispatch loading, allocation of query arrays, constructor marshalling, and host pointer access. Vulkan resource selection remains explicit.
+
+## Ownership and FFI
+
+The native registry stores a tagged union of actual `VkInstance`, `VkPhysicalDevice`, `VkDevice`, `VkBuffer`, `VkDeviceMemory`, or mapping records. Each slot records its generation and parent token. Encode tokens as `U64{slot, generation}`. Reserve zero, retire a slot before generation wrap, and bound-check before indexing. Never cast a token to a pointer or Vulkan handle. Public constructors are not an access-control boundary.
+Every operation checks the token's generation, kind, complete ancestor chain, and required common parent. Repeated queries intern physical devices by instance and actual handle. Physical devices are borrowed records invalidated with their instance. Registry entries retain their parent chain and library lifetime until destruction. Invalid identifiers return `InvalidHandle` before any driver call.
+`Entry` owns `dlopen("libvulkan.so.1")` and global function pointers. Each instance owns a table resolved through `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`; each device owns one resolved through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`. Check required symbols before publishing a token. Keep the loader open until all instances and devices are destroyed. This follows [Vulkan dispatch rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetInstanceProcAddr.html).
+Raw effects have normal constructor arguments and `IO(Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, A>)` results. Each imports `./native.c` and `./native.js`. C uses `io_node` for U64 and wrapper constructors, `io_done` and `io_fail` for results, and `io_cstr` for copied strings. Register reachable effects with `io_eff(CID(Raw.entry_load), entry_load_run, 0)`. Guard each registration with its `CID` and guard shared C definitions against duplicate inclusion. Never use `io_hand` or invent a foreign handle law.
+Generated Bend wrappers decode raw errors into `Error`. Preserve Vulkan result bits exactly as U32, and render their signed value when displaying them. Reserve a disjoint positive code range for wrapper errors and have generation reject collisions with Vulkan result values. Include the failing command and retain unknown VkResult values. Enumeration handles `VK_INCOMPLETE` with bounded retries and an explicit error on exhaustion. Never substitute errno for VkResult.
+Reconstruct each size with `((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo`, and split results in reverse. Use `VkDeviceSize` throughout size, offset, alignment, and bounds calculations. Validate overflow before addition, narrowing to `size_t`, allocation, or pointer arithmetic. Read counts are bounded U32 chunks; offsets and allocations retain all 64 bits. Never use the dependency's signed comparison for unsigned sizes.
+Mapping records keep C pointers plus allocation, offset, and length. Copy operations validate byte values and the requested interval before access. Initially accept only HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT memory for mapping; reject noncoherent mapping explicitly until flush/invalidate support exists. Reject zero sizes, double mapping, rebinding, invalid memory-type selection, and invalid alignment. Check bind requirements against actual registry metadata, following [vkBindBufferMemory](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkBindBufferMemory.html).
+All native operations run synchronously as sequential IO effects on the event-loop thread. The registry has one writer. No Vulkan call enters Bend's pure parallel evaluation or `IO.spawn`. Parallelize independent pure device scoring, payload preparation, and generated-file computations when the work is large enough.
+
+## Cleanup and limited scope
+
+Register resources only after Vulkan creation and required dispatch loading succeed. Roll back unpublished native objects on every later failure. Public destroy/free operations reject live dependents and invalidate tokens after destruction. A duplicate destroy returns `InvalidHandle`; it never reaches Vulkan twice. Dropping a Data wrapper does not destroy its object.
+`Entry.close` is the explicit subtree cleanup operation used by `Entry.with`. Unmap mappings, destroy buffers, free memory, destroy devices, invalidate physical-device records, destroy instances, then close the loader. Continue cleanup after an error, including device loss, and retain diagnostics. A callback failure stays the primary error with cleanup diagnostics appended; a successful callback plus cleanup failure returns `Cleanup`. Close also invalidates every escaped token. Process termination is outside the callback cleanup guarantee.
+The seed accepts exclusive non-sparse buffers, null allocators, no enabled device features/extensions, and null pNext chains. Instance layer/extension names are explicit and checked, including embedded NUL rejection. It exposes wait-idle and destroys only resources it created. It does not support native handle adoption, arbitrary pointers, callbacks, surfaces, swapchains, command submission, or shader execution. JavaScript returns an explicit native-backend-required error.
+
+## Module map and generated growth
+
+`src/vulkan.bend` provides typed public operations and cleanup helpers. `src/types.bend` holds checked configs, errors, and wrapper types. `src/raw.bend` declares effects; `src/native.c` owns the loader, registry, and marshalling. `src/native.js` registers clear unsupported results. `src/generated/vk.bend` contains selected constants and query records; `src/generated/dispatch.inc` contains PFN tables and loaders.
+`tools/generate.py` reads a pinned Khronos `vk.xml` plus `bindings.json`, an allowlist with marshalling and lifecycle policies. Emit supported declarations and dispatch metadata deterministically. Record registry hash, Vulkan header version, and generator command. Reject unsupported pointer shapes instead of generating placeholders. The seed covers only the operations above; add a command by adding its policy and native behavior, then regenerating. Do not pretend that XML alone supplies lifetime or pointer safety.
+`examples/discover.bend`, `examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend`, and `tests/native.bend` use the public API. `LAWS.bend` states pure rules. `PROOF.bend` imports and proves those rules. Pin Bend 2.0.37 because its effect ABI is internal, and compile a constructor/IO smoke test before adding Vulkan calls. The local compiler source confirms the three-argument registration although `bend guide effects` still shows two.
+
+## Verification
+
+Prove unsigned limb ordering, checked range inclusion, and memory-type selection soundness in `LAWS.bend`/`PROOF.bend`. Test C limb conversion with `0`, `2^32`, a mixed high/low pattern, and `2^64-1`; this is ABI evidence, not a Bend proof about foreign code. Run `bend PROOF.bend` before every commit. Native checks build with `bend examples/buffer_roundtrip.bend -o /tmp/vulkan-roundtrip`, then run that binary. The default Bend execution path is JavaScript.
+Use the actual Vulkan loader and an available GPU or software ICD. Require discovery, device creation, buffer allocation/binding, mapping, exact byte roundtrip, and clean teardown. Explicitly report this as host access to Vulkan memory, without claiming GPU work. Test fabricated/stale/wrong-parent tokens, mapping bounds, failed creation rollback, and cleanup with live children. Missing an ICD is a reported integration skip, never a fabricated success. Run validation layers when available and verify the generator produces no diff on a second run.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted and alternatives considered
+
+We accept registry lookups and explicit lifetime errors for constructor-compatible FFI and protection against pointer forgery. We accept a bounded supported subset and copy-based mapped access for a usable first release with clear extension points. Raw pointer-valued U64 handles lose because forged constructors could crash the driver. Affine Type contexts with state returned on every branch expose more ownership plumbing while still allowing drops and fabricated constructors. A monolithic `run_demo` effect hides Vulkan resource decisions and cannot grow into ash-like bindings.
+
+## Open questions, synthesis, and next step
+
+Can CI provide a software ICD and validation layers so native behavior is required on at least one runner? The orchestrator chooses the synthesis; this candidate recommends reusable checked tokens with explicit dispatch and subtree cleanup. Start by compiling the ordinary-constructor roundtrip effect and checking forged-token rejection before implementing Entry loading.
*** End Patch"));

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('/tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-2/design.md')
s = p.read_text()
print(f'{p}: {len(s.splitlines())} lines, {len(s.split())} words')
for needle in ('## Usage', '## Shape', '## Ownership and FFI', '## Cleanup', 'LAWS.bend', 'PROOF.bend', '## Tradeoffs', '## Open questions'):
    assert needle in s, needle
assert s.count('```') % 2 == 0
assert 'io_eff(CID(Raw.entry_load), entry_load_run, 0)' in s
assert 'W.U64{lo: U32, hi: U32}' in s
print('Required sections, constructor ABI, and fenced blocks checked.')
PY","max_output_tokens":1200}); text(r);

content.text: Created [design.md](/tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-2/design.md) with usage, signatures, ownership and FFI rules, cleanup, generation strategy, and alternatives. No repository edits.
